newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar weaker after arbitrage selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar weaker after arbitrage selling.

text.p: White sugar futures headed lower in modest volume as sellers took the chance to sell the nearby August/July differential against New York, traders said on Tuesday.

Spread trading appeared to be the dominant feature of the day's trading. After a lacklustre morning more spreads were traded after the raws opening in New York but London's benchmark August/October was largely ignored and continued to hover around $8.00, they said.
March/May 1998 trades boosted overall turnover and some commission house crosses of October/December were also reported earlier in the session.
Traders said both markets were waiting for a chart gap to be filled in New York between 10.86 and 10.92 cents/lb basis July.
"Until that's filled we probably won't see much more (upside)...that is going to give it a kick start," said one trader.
At 1540 GMT London's spot August contract stood $1.40 lower at $312.50 and October was down 50 cents at $304.40. Volume amounted to 1,087 lots, mostly in the two front months.
Trading was subdued in Paris was limited to 118 lots of the spot August contract, down 40 cents at $312.10.
